meta.source: rules.json — Rule Book products only (LLM-translated from human descriptions, user decision 2026-10-09)
meta.note: Affix table rebuilt to the full Tatabahasa Dewan system (research-verified 2026-10-07 via Kamus Dewan/PRPM). Stripping generates candidates; the DBP lexicon has the final say. Ambiguous branches (meng+V, ter-/di-/ke-/se- vs bare roots) yield multiple candidates, never a verdict. noflag: true entries are exception ranges suppressing overlapping findings from other rule IDs (Rule Book semantics).

rules.desc: Flags the informal pattern 'adjective + sangat' (e.g., 'murah sangat') which should be 'sangat + adjective' in formal Malay.
rules.note: Dalam bahasa formal, 'sangat' patut diletakkan sebelum kata sifat, cth: 'sangat murah', bukan 'murah sangat'.

trigger: Barang ini murah sangat berbanding dengan barang di KL.

rules.impl: The regex matches any single word directly followed by 'sangat' (wrong order, e.g. 'murah sangat'), then cancels the match only when the NEXT word after 'sangat' is one of 60 listed common adjectives (murah, mahal, besar, …) — i.e. correct order ('sangat murah') is recognised by that list alone; an unlisted adjective in correct order (e.g. 'sangat lasak') is a known blind spot that this pattern will wrongly flag. Suggestion swaps the match to 'sangat <matched word>'. Exception: 'sangat sangat' is never flagged.

rules.desc: Flags "kebiasaannya" appearing mid-sentence after a verb, where it should be moved to the front of the sentence.
rules.note: "kebiasaannya" sepatutnya berada di awal ayat, bukan selepas kata kerja. Contoh: "Kebiasaannya, dia datang."

trigger: Mereka makan kebiasaannya pada waktu malam.
Pelajar itu belajar kebiasaannya di perpustakaan.
clear: Kebiasaannya, mereka makan pada waktu malam.

params.judge: Flag the sentence ONLY when 'kebiasaannya' appears mid-sentence AND the word immediately before it is a VERB (an action word like datang, makan, belajar, pergi, tidur, buat) — the adverb has been wrongly placed after the verb. When 'kebiasaannya' appears after a pronoun (dia, mereka, saya, kami, kita, awak, Ali, pelajar itu) or any noun acting as the subject — e.g. 'Dia kebiasaannya datang awal.' — that position is legal: the adverb modifies the whole predicate, do NOT flag. When 'kebiasaannya' is the first word of the sentence (with or without a following comma), do NOT flag. When 'kebiasaannya' follows a preposition or conjunction, treat it as clear. If the preceding word's word class is ambiguous, answer unsure. Example verdicts: 'Dia datang kebiasaannya.' = trigger; 'Mereka makan kebiasaannya pada waktu malam.' = trigger; 'Kebiasaannya, dia datang.' = clear; 'Dia kebiasaannya datang awal.' = clear; 'Pelajar itu belajar kebiasaannya di perpustakaan.' = trigger.

rules.impl: Every sentence is sent to the LLM with this rule's criterion: flag only when 'kebiasaannya' sits mid-sentence directly after a VERB; after a pronoun/noun subject ('Dia kebiasaannya datang awal.') or at the sentence start it is legal and must not be flagged; ambiguous word class answers unsure (never flagged). Flagged sentences get a whole-sentence note (LLM span localisation is not trusted).

rules.desc: Flags 'dari' used after comparison words (lebih/kurang/paling) or 'berasal' for origin, where 'daripada' is required; spares 'dari segi/sudut/aspek/perspektif' (point of view).
rules.note: Gunakan 'daripada' untuk perbandingan (lebih/kurang/paling) dan asal usul (berasal). Contoh: 'lebih tinggi daripada', 'berasal daripada Johor'. Kecualian: 'dari segi/sudut/aspek/perspektif' (sudut pandang) tetap menggunakan 'dari'.

trigger: Harga ini lebih tinggi dari yang itu.
clear: Harga ini lebih tinggi daripada yang itu.
Dari segi kualiti, barang ini bagus.

rules.impl: The regex matches 'lebih/kurang/paling' optionally followed by intervening words then 'dari', or 'berasal dari'; the exception pattern suppresses matches when the word after 'dari' is one of 4 listed point-of-view nouns (segi, sudut, aspek, perspektif).

rules.desc: Flags sentences where lebih or kurang is followed by berbanding (dengan), since comparative forms with lebih/kurang require daripada, not berbanding.
rules.note: Selepas 'lebih' atau 'kurang', gunakan 'daripada', bukan 'berbanding (dengan)'. Contoh: lebih murah daripada barang di KL.

trigger: Kereta ini lebih laju berbanding dengan motosikal.
lebih murah berbanding dengan barang di KL
Harga di sini kurang murah berbanding kedai lain.
clear: Kereta ini lebih laju daripada motosikal.
Berbanding dengan tahun lepas, harga naik.
Berbanding dengan tahun lepas, harga lebih murah.

rules.impl: The regex matches any sentence containing lebih or kurang within 40 characters before berbanding, then suppresses the match when the exception pattern 'berbanding dengan … lebih' is found — i.e. legal fronted 'Berbanding dengan … lebih …' clauses are skipped.

rules.desc: Flags sentences where 'kepada' follows benefit/purpose nouns like faedah, manfaat, habis, or ruang, since 'bagi' should be used instead.
rules.note: Gunakan 'bagi' (bukan 'kepada') selepas kata seperti faedah, manfaat, habis, dan ruang yang menyatakan manfaat atau tujuan.

trigger: Manfaat program ini kepada masyarakat setempat.
clear: Manfaat program ini bagi masyarakat setempat.

rules.impl: The regex matches any of four benefit nouns (faedah, manfaat, habis, ruang) followed within 30 characters by kepada, then suppresses the match when the span also contains one of 5 listed giver verbs (memberi, memberikan, beri, berikan, mengurniakan) — i.e. legal 'X kepada Y' recipient constructions are recognised by that verb list only.

rules.desc: Flags incorrect time prepositions: 'dalam' before specific time points (bulan/tahun/tarikh/saat/waktu), 'pada' before duration words (tempoh), and 'di' before time expressions (saat/waktu/bulan/tahun/tarikh).
rules.note: Kesalahan kata depan waktu. Gunakan 'pada' untuk titik masa (bulan/tahun/tarikh/saat/waktu), 'dalam' untuk tempoh, dan 'di' hanya untuk tempat.

trigger: Di saat dia sampai, semua diam.
clear: Pada saat dia sampai, semua diam.

rules.impl: The regex matches three specific error patterns: 'dalam' directly followed by one of five time-point nouns (bulan, tahun, tarikh, saat, waktu), 'pada' directly followed by 'tempoh', and 'di' directly followed by one of the same five time nouns. No exceptions are defined.

rules.desc: Flags the copula 'adalah' when directly followed by a verb phrase (passive verb, 'merupakan', or other verbs), which is ungrammatical in Malay.
rules.note: Adalah sebagai pemeri tidak boleh diikuti oleh frasa kerja. Buang 'adalah' atau ubah struktur ayat. Contoh: 'Dimaklumkan bahawa...' bukan 'Adalah dimaklumkan bahawa...'. Untuk 'adalah merupakan', gunakan 'merupakan' sahaja.

trigger: Adalah dimaklumkan bahawa majlis akan diadakan.
Perkara ini adalah dilakukan oleh pihak pengurusan.

rules.impl: The regex matches the word 'adalah' followed by whitespace and then either the word 'merupakan' or any word starting with 'di' and ending in 'kan', 'h', or 'i' (covering common passive verbs like dimaklumkan, dilakukan, diadakan, disahkan, dll). No exceptions are defined.

rules.desc: Flags the incorrect meN- prefix realisation 'mensetujui' before a root starting with 's', where the correct form is 'menyetujui' (meN- + s-root → meny- + s-root).
rules.note: Bentuk yang betul ialah 'menyetujui' (meN- + kata dasar bermula dengan s → meny-). Anda juga boleh menggunakan 'bersetuju dengan'.
rules.impl: The regex matches the exact word 'mensetujui' (case-insensitive, with word boundaries on both sides) and suggests replacing it with 'menyetujui'.

rules.desc: Flags 'memberikan' when directly followed by an animate recipient noun (with or without the -nya clitic) or 'mereka', since plain 'memberi' should be used for giving to people.
rules.note: Gunakan 'memberi' (bukan 'memberikan') apabila penerima adalah manusia: memberi pelajar, memberi anaknya, memberi mereka.

clear: Dia memberikan bantuan kepada mangsa banjir.

params.judge: Flag the sentence when the verb 'memberikan' is directly followed by a LIVING recipient — a person or animate being, including possessive clitic forms (anaknya, gurunya, rakan-rakan) and pronouns referring to people (mereka, kami). With a living recipient the correct form is plain 'memberi': 'Guru memberi pelajar sebuah buku.', 'Ibu memberi anaknya coklat.' Do NOT flag when 'memberikan' is followed by an inanimate thing (sumbangan, bantuan, nasihat, layanan, taklimat...) — that is correct: 'Dia memberikan sumbangan besar.' If the following noun's animacy is genuinely ambiguous, answer unsure. Example verdicts: 'Ibu memberikan anaknya coklat.' = trigger; 'Guru memberikan murid buku.' = trigger; 'Dia memberikan sumbangan besar.' = clear; 'Pihak syarikat memberikan taklimat kepada media.' = clear.

rules.impl: Every sentence is sent to the LLM with this rule's criterion: flag 'memberikan' only when its direct object is a living recipient (person/animal, incl. -nya clitics and people-pronouns) where plain 'memberi' is required; 'memberikan' with an inanimate object (sumbangan/bantuan/nasihat...) is correct and must not be flagged; ambiguous animacy answers unsure (never flagged). Flagged sentences get a whole-sentence note (LLM span localisation is not trusted).

rules.desc: Flags coordinated lists (comma/and-series) that mix fully-affixed verbs with bare nouns, breaking parallel verb-phrase structure.
rules.note: Senarai selari tidak seimbang: jangan campurkan kata kerja terbitan dengan kata nama kasar dalam satu siri. Pastikan semua item mempunyai bentuk yang sama.

trigger: Aktiviti itu merangkumi bergotong-royong, kuih-muih, dan menyanyi.
clear: Aktiviti itu merangkumi bergotong-royong, memasak, dan menyanyi.

params.judge: A sentence violates this rule if it contains a coordinated series (items separated by commas and/or 'dan') where the items mix fully-affixed verbs (e.g., bergotong-royong, menyanyi, memasak, bermain) with bare nouns (e.g., kuih-muih, makanan, permainan). Every item in such a verb series should be a verb with parallel form; a single bare noun item inside a verb series is a violation. Lists that are consistently all nouns (no verbs present) are fine and must NOT be flagged. Lists that are consistently all verbs are fine. Only flag when a bare noun appears among verbs in the same coordinated series.
params.suggestion: Gantikan kata nama kasar dengan kata kerja yang selaras, atau asingkan kata nama ke dalam senarai berasingan.

rules.impl: Every sentence is sent to the LLM with the criterion: flag coordinated series that mix fully-affixed verbs with bare nouns, sparing all-noun or all-verb lists; sentences the LLM calls trigger are flagged as a whole-sentence note.

rules.desc: Flags doubled copulas (adalah merupakan, ialah merupakan, ialah ialah, adalah adalah) and double adversative conjunctions (tetapi ... namun, walaupun ... tetapi) in the same sentence.
rules.note: Penggunaan kata bersamaan secara berlebihan (kembar kata) tidak gramatis. Padam salah satu kata hubung/kopula yang berlebihan.

trigger: Dia datang tetapi dia tidak bercakap namun dia tersenyum.
clear: Dia datang tetapi dia tidak bercakap.

rules.impl: The regex matches four exact doubled-copula phrases (adalah merupakan, ialah merupakan, ialah ialah, adalah adalah) as contiguous word pairs, and also matches three cross-sentence double-conjunction patterns by searching for the first conjunction then any non-period characters then the second conjunction (tetapi…namun, namun…tetapi, walaupun…tetapi).

rules.desc: Flags plural markers (sebahagian, beberapa, para, semua, kebanyakan) directly followed by a reduplicated noun, which is redundant.
rules.note: Penanda jamak seperti 'beberapa', 'para', 'semua', 'sebahagian', dan 'kebanyakan' sudah menyatakan jamak. Tidak perlu ulang kata nama selepasnya. Contoh: 'beberapa orang' (bukan 'beberapa orang-orang').

trigger: Kebanyakan guru-guru bersetuju dengan cadangan itu.
clear: Kebanyakan guru bersetuju dengan cadangan itu.

rules.impl: The regex matches any of the five plural markers followed by whitespace and a reduplicated noun (word-hyphen-same-word), capturing the noun in group 2 and back-referencing it to confirm exact reduplication. No exceptions are needed since the pattern is already narrow — it only fires on true reduplication, not on hyphenated compounds.

rules.desc: Flags calqued English phrases 'kerana fakta bahawa' (due to the fact that) and 'adalah kerana' in Malay.
rules.note: Frasa ini dipinjam terjemah daripada bahasa Inggeris. Ganti 'kerana fakta bahawa' dengan 'kerana'. Ganti 'adalah kerana' dengan 'ialah kerana' atau ubah struktur ayat.

trigger: Hal ini berlaku kerana fakta bahawa harga naik.
clear: Hal ini berlaku kerana harga naik.

rules.impl: The regex matches two calqued phrases: 'kerana fakta bahawa' (any whitespace between the three words) and 'adalah kerana' (any whitespace between the two words). No exceptions are defined.

rules.desc: Flags the English calques 'yang mana' and 'di mana' when used as relative pronouns or conjunctions inside a statement, while sparing interrogative 'Di mana' at sentence start.
rules.note: Penggunaan 'yang mana' atau 'di mana' sebagai kata hubung relatif ialah calque bahasa Inggeris. Gantikan dengan 'yang' atau 'tempat' mengikut konteks.

trigger: Buku yang mana saya beli itu mahal.
Laporan yang mana dikemukakan semalam telah diluluskan.
Mesyuarat di mana keputusan dibuat adalah rahsia.
Sekolah di mana dia belajar terletak di bandar.
clear: Laporan yang dikemukakan semalam telah diluluskan.
Buku yang saya beli itu mahal.

rules.impl: The regex matches 'yang mana' anywhere, and 'di mana' except in two contexts: at the start of a sentence (a location question like 'Di mana kamu tinggal?') or anywhere in a sentence that ends with a question mark (e.g. 'Kamu tinggal di mana?'). Relative-conjunction uses ('Mesyuarat di mana keputusan dibuat...') are flagged. Embedded questions in statements ('Dia tanya di mana stesen.') are still flagged — only direct questions are exempt.

rules.desc: Flags three Malay collocation errors: 'menggapai untung' (should be 'meraih untung'), 'terima kasih di atas' for gratitude (should be 'terima kasih atas'), and 'menyambungkan talian kepada' with non-living objects (should use 'dengan').
rules.note: Ralat kolokasi. Untung diraih/bukan digapai. Ucapan terima kasih menggunakan 'atas' (bukan 'di atas' yang hanya untuk ruang). Untuk objek bukan hidup guna 'dengan' bukan 'kepada'.

trigger: Syarikat itu berjaya menggapai untung besar.
Terima kasih di atas sokongan anda.
Syarikat itu menyambungkan talian kepada pelanggan.
clear: Syarikat itu berjaya meraih untung besar.
Syarikat itu menyambungkan talian dengan pelanggan.

rules.impl: The regex matches three specific collocation patterns: 'menggapai untung', 'terima kasih di atas', and 'menyambungkan talian kepada' — each flagged as a collocation error with no exceptions.

rules.desc: Flags the misspellings 'frekuensy' (should be 'frekuensi') and 'membantuh' (should be 'membantu').
rules.impl: The regex matches whole-word 'frekuensy' or 'membantuh' (case-insensitive) with no exceptions; any match is flagged as a spelling error.

rules.desc: Flags the bare verb 'lepas' directly followed by a noun phrase object (should be 'lepaskan'), while sparing prepositional/conjunctional uses like 'lepas makan' or 'selepas'.
rules.note: Frasa "lepas" + objek dalam konteks ini adalah bahasa basahan. Gunakan "lepaskan" untuk maksud melepaskan sesuatu objek.

trigger: Dia lepas burung itu pagi tadi.
clear: Dia lepaskan burung itu pagi tadi.

rules.impl: The regex matches the word 'lepas' followed by whitespace and any word, but uses a negative lookahead to skip common prepositional contexts ('lepas makan', 'lepas itu', 'lepas kami', etc.); the exceptions pattern additionally suppresses any match containing 'selepas'.
